title: {{NAME}} and the Lost Foal
moral: A gentle heart can find magic in the most ordinary places.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a gentle young girl with long curly auburn hair and violet eyes, wearing a lavender dress with tiny stars, white knee-high socks, and silver ballet flats — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} spotted the trail on a Tuesday evening — a line of tiny silver hoofprints glittering in the grass, leading from the garden gate all the way to the rose bushes.

She followed them very slowly, the way you move when you don't want to frighten something.

Under the tallest rosebush, tangled in a loop of thorny stem, was a unicorn foal. She was very small, pale gold, with a spiral horn no bigger than a pencil. She looked up at {{NAME}} with enormous dark eyes and made the tiniest sound imaginable.

No text, no words, no letters anywhere in the image.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} sat very still and spoke in her quietest voice.

"Hello. I won't hurt you. I'm going to help."

The foal's ears flicked forward. She didn't pull away.

Very carefully, {{NAME}} worked each thorn loose — one at a time, gentle as threading a needle. It took a long time. When the last thorn came free, the foal shook herself, sneezed a tiny shower of silver sparks, and stepped into {{NAME}}'s arms.

She weighed almost nothing at all, like holding a warm dream.

pages.content:
The foal nudged {{NAME}}'s hand and then turned, walking deeper into the garden.

"You want me to follow?" asked {{NAME}}.

The foal looked back once — and {{NAME}} was sure she smiled.

They walked past the vegetable patch and the old stone wall and through a gap in the hedge {{NAME}} had never noticed before. On the other side was a meadow she had definitely never seen — wide and silver-lit, full of flowers that seemed to grow in slow motion.

pages.content:
In the centre of the meadow, a herd of unicorns stood perfectly still, their horns catching the moonlight.

The largest one — pearl-white, mane like seafoam — stepped forward. The foal ran to her and disappeared under her neck, making a sound of pure relief.

The mother unicorn dipped her horn toward {{NAME}}. A soft light bloomed at the tip and drifted down like a petal, landing on {{NAME}}'s left hand.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} looked at her hand. A tiny star — no bigger than a freckle — was glowing softly on her palm.

She walked home through the hedge, and when she looked back, the gap was just a gap again. An ordinary gap.

But the star on her hand stayed. Even after her bath. Even after she got into bed and turned off the light.

In the dark, it glowed just enough to wish on.

{{NAME}} made her wish, closed her hand gently, and fell fast asleep.
